title: SDK surface spec: resumable iterators, ergonomic retries, and language parity
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD-style specification for a unified SDK surface across Python, TypeScript, and Go that provides: resumable pagination/streaming iterators, ergonomic retry/backoff configuration, explicit idempotency controls, and a clear compatibility/deprecation policy. Goal is to reduce integration complexity for customers who switch runtimes or update Redwood backend semantics and to minimize client-side boilerplate for safe resume after transient failures.
goals: Provide a single high-level iterator abstraction that supports both paginated REST endpoints and streaming token/chunk responses with resume semantics
Expose a minimal retry/backoff API that is consistent across languages and integrates with existing client-side hooks (cancellation, timeouts)
Document compatibility guarantees and deprecation windows for iterator semantics, cursor formats, and retry idempotency markers
non_goals: Ship a breaking redesign of current generated SDK methods; aim for adapters/compatibility shims instead
Enforce a single networking stack implementation across languages; allow language-idiomatic implementations behind the spec
constraints: Must be implementable without requiring major infra changes in the next two releases. Cursor token sizes should remain <= 4KB when possible. Backward-compatible server-side changes only; clients must be able to opt into new behaviors via header or version flag.
scope: Include client-side surface (iterator APIs, retry config, helper utilities), acceptance tests per-language, example migration guides, and a compatibility matrix. Exclude changes to the server-side cursor encoding until the compatibility window is announced.
design_decisions: Use explicit Cursor object returned from list endpoints instead of opaque strings where feasible (server still supports opaque string fallback)
Iterator API provides async/await friendly streams (Python async iterator, TS AsyncIterable, Go channel-based iterator) and also sync convenience wrappers
Retry API uses a small struct: {mode: "standard|aggressive|none", max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter: "full|none"} - wire-level behavior documented in helper docs
compatibility_policy: Minor SDK versions may add ergonomic helpers but cannot change iterator resume semantics for at least 180 days after release. Cursor token format is considered stable for 360 days; if we change it, the server will continue to accept deprecated tokens for the window and return a 'migrated_cursor' hint when possible. Breaking changes require a migration guide, explicit opt-in header, and a deprecation notice in release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Python, TS, and Go SDKs all expose a 'resumable_iterator' surface with identical behavioral tests in CI
When client receives 5xx (transient) while streaming, iterator must attempt configured retries without emitting duplicated user-visible items (idempotent semantics verified)
When iterator is paused/crashed and resumed with the last-seen cursor, the SDK resumes from the next unseen item with no duplicates or gaps in a 99.99% of synthetic test runs
Documentation includes migration guide, code samples for each language, and a compatibility table mapping server flags to client toggles
Performance: iterator overhead measured in microbenchmarks shows <5% additional latency per item relative to current baseline for small pages (<= 100 tokens / 50 items)
test_plan: Create a matrix of tests: network flakiness simulation (latency, resets, partial payloads), cursor expiry cases, non-idempotent operation markers, and large result sets. Implement language-agnostic golden tests that assert exact sequence of items emitted given a replayed set of server events. Add integration tests against dedicated Canary deployment and run on PRs for SDKs.
acceptance_examples: Python: async for item in client.resumable_iterator.list_messages(conversation_id=cid, page_size=50, retry=Retry.standard()): process(item)
TS: for await (const item of client.iterator.listMessages({conversationId: cid, pageSize: 50}, {retry: Retry.standard()})) { process(item) }
Go: it := client.ListMessages(ctx, opts); for it.Next() { item := it.Value(); process(item) }
edge_cases_and_risks: Cursor drift when server-side pruning removes events referenced by an old cursor - mitigation: server returns 'cursor_unavailable' and iterator yields a well-documented RecoverableCursorError with recommended fallback (full list re-scan)
Partial stream frames where connection drops after headers - SDK must be able to resume using last-acknowledged index if server supports event indexes; otherwise retry whole chunk
Non-idempotent operations surfaced via iterators (rare) — require explicit to_mark_non_idempotent flag and prevent automatic retries by default
telemetry_and_observability: SDKs will emit standardized telemetry events: iterator.started, iterator.page_fetched (page_size), iterator.retry (attempt, reason), iterator.resumed (cursor_age_ms), iterator.error (code). Events must include SDK version, runtime, and optional customer-supplied metadata. Telemetry payloads follow existing SDK telemetry endpoint conventions.
migration_steps: 1) Publish spec and code examples. 2) Implement shims in each SDK that translate new iterator calls to existing endpoints; opt-in via client flag. 3) Run canary tests with 10 internal customers. 4) Announce GA and deprecation window for legacy cursor-only resume code paths. 5) After 360 days of compatibility window, roll forward server cursor change behind opt-in header, continue supporting legacy tokens for the remainder of window.
implementation_notes: Eng teams should prioritize a small adapter layer so generated SDKs don't need full rewrite. Ensure cancellation semantics (context in Go, AbortSignal in TS, asyncio.CancelledError in Python) propagate cleanly. Provide helper Retry presets and allow override via function parameter. Add unit tests that assert no duplication on resume by simulating interleaved ACKs.
